title: The Island stopped being a diagram of a place
thesis: The same opening beat — you wash up on a shore beneath a lighthouse — told three ways: as a flat picture you clicked through, as a world you could walk but not believe, and as somewhere that behaves like a place while you stand in it.
summary: In February The Island was a 2D SVG point-and-click: flat shapes, arrow buttons, one still frame per location. June replaced it wholesale with ABYME, a walkable 3D island. What followed was the harder half — giving that world surfaces, weather, wildlife and depth, so it stopped reading as untextured geometry.

before.label: Earlier builds — Feb SVG, Jun first-3D

comparisons.title: From a picture of a beach to a beach
comparisons.caption: Both are the opening location. February was a 2D SVG scene: flat fills, a circle for the moon, triangles for trees, and arrow buttons to step between static frames — you looked at the island rather than stood on it. Today the same beat is a first-person world you walk with WASD, and the line that greets you is unchanged: the tide brought you back.

before.alt: The Island in February: a flat 2D SVG night scene of a beach with a circular moon, triangular trees and directional arrow buttons beneath it.

after.alt: The Island today: a first-person 3D shore with wet pebbles, driftwood, gulls standing at the waterline and a lighthouse in haze beyond the treeline.

comparisons.title: The world was built in June; the surfaces took the rest of the summer
comparisons.caption: Left is the first playable 3D build (afc3b6b4, 11 June) from the same spawn point, once its opening camera hands over. The geometry and the composition were already right — the lighthouse sits where it sits now. What it had no answer for was surface: bare flat-shaded sand, spiky grass standing in for undergrowth, an empty shoreline. The right-hand frame is the same view after the texturing and life passes: pebble shingle at the tideline, driftwood, layered vegetation, gulls, and haze doing the work of distance.

before.alt: The first 3D build of The Island: flat-shaded low-poly terrain with bare sand, sparse spiky grass and no wildlife, under a plain sky.

after.alt: The same view today: textured pebble shingle, driftwood, denser vegetation, gulls at the waterline and atmospheric haze around the lighthouse.

changes.title: The medium changed, not just the art
changes.body: February's build could only ever show you a location. ABYME replaced the SVG scene graph with a real-time 3D world, which turns the same puzzle content into a place you occupy — you find things by looking around rather than by exhausting the clickable regions of a frame.

changes.title: Surfaces stopped being flat colour
changes.body: The first 3D pass shipped untextured, which is why it read as a model rather than a shore. The fix was relief rather than tiled colour: normal maps derived from generated height, so stone, sand and bark catch raking light while the palette stays under the era grade's control. Tiled colour was tried and rejected — at arm's length it pixelated into a grid.

changes.title: The island got inhabitants and weather
changes.body: Gulls and crows that land, perch and take off; a tide that moves; light that travels through the day. Motion is what separates a diorama from a place, and most of it is incidental rather than scripted — it happens whether or not you are watching.

changes.title: It became something you can finish
changes.body: Behind the view there is now a save format under contract, a notebook that records what you have actually seen, and an executable walk that drives the whole game end to end in CI — so the story can be completed, and can be proven to still complete after every change.

builderNote.quote: I really want to be wow'd.
builderNote.context: The owner's standing bar for this game, recorded verbatim in its quality-loop mission doc, and the reason this is published rather than filed as finished. The Feb-to-now leap is the easy story — changing medium always looks dramatic. The June-to-now comparison is the one that matters, because it is four months of work on surfaces and life that never shows up as a new feature.

proof.label: Captured
proof.value: All three builds driven through their real Begin gate at the same spawn, with the opening camera allowed to hand over — no debug flythrough or posed camera.

proof.label: February
proof.value: 0ec63afa, 2 Feb 2026 — 2D SVG point-and-click, one still frame per location.

proof.label: First 3D
proof.value: afc3b6b4, 11 Jun 2026 — walkable world, untextured; its opening camera runs 21 seconds before it hands you the controls.

proof.label: Today
proof.value: 4ee44681, 4 Sep 2026 — textured surfaces, wildlife, tide and day cycle, with an end-to-end walk gate in CI.

share.summary: The same opening beach, three ways: a flat SVG frame you clicked through, an untextured 3D model you could walk, and a shore with pebbles, gulls and weather.
